source.title: Recent Results and Open Problems on the Hydrodynamics of Disordered Asymmetric Exclusion and Zero-Range Processes

accepted.question_text: Consider a disordered asymmetric zero-range process on Z^d in which each site x has a random jump-rate multiplier alpha_x in [c,1], particles at x jump out at rate alpha_x r(eta(x)), and the jump kernel is asymmetric with nonzero drift. For this model, Benjamini, Ferrari, and Landim proved a hydrodynamic limit only under assumptions that exclude the phase-transition regime, so the result does not describe initial macroscopic densities above the critical density rho^*. The open question is to determine the hydrodynamic behavior when the initial density profile satisfies rho > rho^* somewhere, or equivalently to extend the high-density hydrodynamic theorem now known for the special one-dimensional totally asymmetric model with r(k)=1_{k>=1} to more general zero-range processes.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Extend Theorem 1 to describe hydrodynamic behavior also at high density ρ > ρ∗. Or, equivalently, extend Theorem 2 to more general ZRP’s.
The shortcoming of this result is that it does not indicate what happens on the hydrodynamic scale if the process starts at density above critical, that is, u0(x) > ρ∗ for some or all x.

accepted.question_text: Assume the disordered zero-range process is in the phase-transition regime with finite critical density rho^*. The known hydrodynamic theorem implies that when the initial density is everywhere above rho^*, the macroscopic profile stays fixed on the hydrodynamic scale because the flux is constant there. The open problem is to prove rigorous finer-scale results beyond this trivial hydrodynamic picture, specifically to show whether inhomogeneities form and particles concentrate on exceptionally slow sites when the density is in the high-density regime rho > rho^*.
accepted.context_brief: Finer-scale phase-transition behavior in disordered ZRP

evidence.quote: Problem 2. In the phase transition case, the hydrodynamic theorem reveals only trivial behavior at high density ρ > ρ∗ (the profile does not move, see Theorem 2). It is expected that on a finer space scale one can see inhomogeneities develop, specifically, that the particles concentrate on exceptionally slow sites. No rigorous results exist to decribe these phenomena.

In the phase transition case this theorem has an interesting consequence: Suppose the initial profile satifies u0(x) ≥ ρ∗ everywhere on R. Then since f is constant for this range of densities, it follows that u(x, t) = u0(x) for all t > 0. In other words, the profile does not change on the hydrodynamic scale.

accepted.question_text: Fix a realization of the site disorder alpha for a disordered zero-range process, and start the process from a spatially ergodic initial distribution of density rho. Let nu^alpha_phi denote the explicit family of invariant product measures for this model, and let rho^* be the critical density when the phase transition occurs. The open question is whether the law of the process eta(t) converges weakly as t tends to infinity to an equilibrium measure nu^alpha_phi determined by the density, and in the phase-transition case with rho > rho^*, whether eta(t) instead converges weakly to the equilibrium state with density rho^*.
accepted.context_brief: Weak convergence to equilibrium for disordered ZRP

evidence.quote: Problem 3. An interesting open problem for the disordered ZRP concerns the weak convergence of the process: Fix the rates α, and take the initial distribution of η(0) spatially ergodic with density ρ. Does the distribution of η(t) converge weakly, as t → ∞, to one of the equilibria ναϕ? If ρ > ρ∗ in the phase transition case, does η(t) converge weakly to the equilibrium with density ρ∗?

accepted.question_text: For the disordered totally asymmetric simple exclusion process, and more generally the one-dimensional totally asymmetric K-exclusion process with site disorder where each site can hold at most K particles and the macroscopic limit has an unknown concave flux function f_K on [0,K], determine whether the model exhibits a phase transition analogous to the disordered zero-range process. A specific open question is whether the flux function f_K(rho) contains a flat segment on an interval centered around rho = K/2.
accepted.context_brief: Phase transition and flux shape for disordered TASEP/K-exclusion

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For the disordered TASEP, any new rigorous results would be welcome. For example, is there a phase transition similar to the one for disordered ZRP? Does the flux function fK(ρ) have a flat segment on an interval around ρ = K/2?

The disordered SEP is less well understood than the ZRP. The reason is that no invariant distributions have been found. Presently we can prove the existence of a hydrodynamic limit for the totally asymmetric SEP, in dimension one. But the flux function f of the macroscopic equation (2.18) remains unknown. The theorem covers a more general totally asymmetric SEP, namely the so-called K-exclusion, where each site admits K particles instead of just one.
